title: Longest Run of Consecutive Values

concept.title: Start counting only at the beginning of a run
body: Find the longest set of values `x, x+1, x+2, ...` that all occur in the array (in any order, positions do not matter). Sorting works in O(n log n), but a hash set does it in O(n). Put all values in a set. A value `x` is the **start of a run** exactly when `x - 1` is not in the set. From each start, count upward while `y + 1` is in the set.

body.code:
present = set(a)
best = 0
for x in present:
    if x - 1 not in present:          # x starts a run
        y = x
        while y + 1 in present: y += 1
        best = max(best, y - x + 1)

body: Because we only start at run beginnings, every value is visited at most twice (once in the loop, once while counting), so the total work is linear even though there is a loop inside the loop.

statement: Given `n` integers (duplicates are possible), find the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integer values `x, x+1, ..., x+L-1` that all appear in the array. The order of the elements in the array does not matter.
hints: Put all numbers in a set.
A number starts a run when the number one smaller is not in the set.
From each start count upward, and remember the longest run.

explanation: Only the first value of every run starts a count. Each value is then touched a constant number of times.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

present = set(a)
best = 0
for x in present:
    if x - 1 not in present:
        y = x
        while y + 1 in present:
            y += 1
        best = max(best, y - x + 1)
print(best)
